app-channels:
A **destination** is a marketplace or advertising site where you want to list vehicles. You manage destinations on **Channels**.

## Complete setup

1. Choose the destination you want to use.
2. Follow the next action shown. This may mean signing in, entering account details or contacting that company.
3. Check which delivery method is available. Some destinations need manual work or partner approval.
4. Review the vehicles you want to list. Missing prices, photos or other required details can prevent publication.

Connecting an account does not enable automatic updates by itself. Only destinations available for automatic updates can be selected in Autopilot.

## Understand the result

| Label or result | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| Connected | Account setup is recorded. Check the delivery method and any remaining steps. |
| Sent or submitted | An update was sent. The destination may still need to process it. |
| Confirmed live | DealerGrid has a current confirmation that the listing is visible. |
| Needs attention | Read the reason and next action. The task may belong to you, support or the destination company. |

Auto Marketplace is DealerGrid’s own consumer website. External sites have their own accounts, rules and processing times. A setup guide or connection does not mean DealerGrid can automatically publish to that site.

Read [Automatic updates and pausing](doc:processes/auto-sync) or [Why a website has not updated](doc:app/sync-vs-accounts).
app-getting-started:
Use the dealership name at the top of the page to confirm which business you are working on.

## Your daily screens

- **Home:** see what needs your attention and choose the next task.
- **Vehicles:** add stock, correct details and photos, and mark vehicles sold or removed.
- **Channels:** choose marketplace and advertising sites, complete their setup, and check listing results.
- **Leads:** follow up on buyer inquiries received by DealerGrid. Your team shares the status and notes.

Use **Settings** for dealership details, team access and notification preferences. **Reports** contains additional information about inventory and activity.

## Get help without leaving your work

Choose **Help** in the header. It opens relevant documentation in a separate tab, leaving your work in place. Search the documentation index for other questions, or follow related articles and tags. Close the documentation tab to return to your original screen.

## Know what has actually happened

A vehicle can be saved without being listed. A destination can be connected without a listing being live. Check the listing result on Channels before assuming a website has changed.

Read [Connect a destination](doc:app/channels), [Prepare a vehicle for listing](doc:inventory/inventory-readiness), or [Manage buyer inquiries](doc:app/lead-status).
app-lead-status:
On Leads, mark each inquiry **New**, **Contacted**, **Appointment**, **Closed / Won**, or **Lost**. Your team sees the same status. Buyers never see it. It does not change listings.

## When to use each one

| Status | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| New | Nobody has followed up yet |
| Contacted | You reached the buyer |
| Appointment | A visit or call is booked |
| Closed / Won | The deal is done |
| Lost | The buyer went elsewhere or stopped answering |

## What happens next

A new inquiry starts as **New**. Change it when you take the next step. The rest of the team sees that change in this inbox.

The inbox and delivery results are separate. Open **Leads → Delivery log** to review recorded notifications. Configure alerts in **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries**. An inquiry appearing in the inbox does not confirm an email was delivered.

## Send an inquiry to your CRM

A customer relationship management system (CRM) is separate from the shared inbox. Use the inquiry’s **Send to CRM** action to review its destination and delivery result. Acceptance by the mail server does not confirm that the CRM imported the inquiry. If sending is unavailable, read the reason and use the copy or export options shown. Changing a lead status does not send it to the CRM.

Read [Choose how you hear about new inquiries](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
app-reports:
Open **Reports** from the dealership header. Choose the report that matches the question you are trying to answer, then check the dealership and date range.

## Before acting on a number

- Check when the data was last updated.
- Read the labels: inventory totals, sent updates and confirmed live listings measure different things.
- An empty report may mean there are no matching records or the data is not available. It does not prove there were no problems.
- Use the relevant vehicle, lead or destination page to make changes.

For a listing problem, start with [Why a website has not updated](doc:app/sync-vs-accounts). For price suggestions based on time in stock, read [Review older inventory](doc:inventory/older-inventory).
app-sync-vs-accounts:
If a listing did not change, decide which of two things is unfinished: the vehicle, or the destination.

## Start with Vehicles

Open Vehicles when the question is “can this unit be listed?” Missing price, photos, or other required details can stop an update. Also check that availability is correct: a sold vehicle still marked available can continue to be advertised.

## Then open Channels

Open Channels when the question is “can we send to this site?” A destination that is not connected, needs sign-in, or is waiting on the partner will not receive updates — even if every vehicle looks complete.

## Order of work

1. Fix the vehicle details that Vehicles says are missing.
2. Check the destination on Channels. Finish setup and confirm its update method. For automatic updates, check that Autopilot is on and the destination is selected.
3. Confirm the last update went through. Connected does not mean the site already shows the change.

Fixing vehicles does not connect a destination. Connecting a destination does not fill in a missing VIN.
app-team-access:
A dealership owner can manage teammates in **Settings → Team**. Internal staff use **People & access** in the dealership record. Available actions depend on your role.

## Invite someone

Check the person’s email and role before creating the invitation. Then read the delivery result:

- **Email sent:** the mail server accepted the message. If it does not arrive, ask the person to check their spam folder and confirm the address.
- **Link created:** email delivery is not configured. Copy the setup link and share it with the intended person.
- **Email failed:** the message was not sent successfully. Check the address and follow the retry or link-sharing option shown.

Resending creates a new setup link and invalidates the old one. Share the newest link.

## Accept an invitation

Open the setup link. New users choose a password. If you already have a DealerGrid account, enter that account’s password to accept access to the additional dealership.

If the link expired or was revoked, ask the person who invited you for a new one. An invitation does not let you view another person’s password.

## Temporary passwords and other sign-in problems

If staff gave you a temporary password, sign in with it and choose your own password before continuing. If your account is suspended, ask the dealership owner or internal support to review access. For a forgotten password, ask an authorized administrator to use the available recovery action; do not create a duplicate account.

If you can sign in but cannot find a dealership, ask the owner or internal support to check your dealership assignment.
connections-auto-response:
Auto-Response attempts to send an acknowledgment after a new inquiry. It does not replace your team’s follow-up or guarantee delivery.

## What to do

1. Open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**.
2. Turn on Auto-Response. It stays off until you do this.
3. Choose email, text, or both. Text also needs the buyer’s phone and texting enabled by support.
4. Keep the default message or write your own with `{name}`, `{vehicle}`, and `{dealer}`.

## What happens next

The inquiry is saved before delivery is attempted. Review recorded results and failures in **Leads → Delivery log**. Auto-Response only runs on the first inquiry — it does not answer follow-ups.

Keep texts short. Ask your compliance contact before you turn this on in your state.
connections-discord:
Discord posts each new inquiry as a card in the channel you choose.

## What to do

In DealerGrid, open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**.

1. In Discord, open the server and choose the channel.
2. Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook.
3. Copy the webhook URL.
4. In DealerGrid, open How you hear about new inquiries, paste the URL, and save.

The next inquiry posts to that channel with stock number, destination, and buyer details.

To change channels, create a new webhook there and replace the URL. To stop Discord alerts, clear the URL and save.

See [Choose how you hear about new inquiries](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
connections-email-notifications:
Email alerts go to the **email** on your dealership’s primary contact. You do not set up a separate mailbox.

## What to do

In DealerGrid, open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**.

1. Confirm the primary contact email in Settings.
2. Leave email enabled if you want alerts, or turn it off and save if you do not.

## What the message includes

The subject names the stock number. The body has the destination, vehicle, buyer name, email, phone, and message. Blank buyer fields are omitted.

## If mail is not arriving

- Check the primary contact email.
- Check junk. First messages from a new sender often land there.
- Ask support if nothing has ever arrived and junk is not the cause.

See [Choose how you hear about new inquiries](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
connections-lead-notifications:
When a buyer asks about a vehicle, DealerGrid can notify every method you turned on. One method failing does not stop the others.

## What to do

Open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**. Add only what your team will use, then save. Internal staff can use the same section in the dealership profile.

| Method | What you add | Who sets it up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email | Primary contact email on the dealership profile | You |
| Discord | A webhook URL from your Discord channel | You |
| Telegram | A bot token and chat ID | You |
| Webhook | An HTTPS address that accepts a POST | You or your integrator |
| SMS | A mobile number | You, after support enables texting |

## What you receive

Email and integration alerts can include vehicle and buyer details; SMS contains a shorter summary. Check **Leads → Delivery log** for recorded delivery outcomes. A saved setting does not confirm delivery, and acceptance by a mail server does not confirm that someone read the message.

[Email](doc:connections/email-notifications) · [Discord](doc:connections/discord) · [Telegram](doc:connections/telegram) · [SMS](doc:connections/sms) · [Webhook](doc:connections/webhook)
connections-sms:
A text is a short alert when a new inquiry arrives, for example: “New lead from Alex Johnson for Stock #DM-2024-042. Log in to respond.”

## What to do

In DealerGrid, open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**.

1. Enter one mobile number using country code, no spaces: `+15551234567`.
2. Save. Ask support to confirm texting is enabled for your dealership.

Until support enables it, the number is saved but texts are not sent. One number is used per dealership. To reach several people, use a shared number that forwards to the team.

To stop texts, clear the number and save.

See [Choose how you hear about new inquiries](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
connections-telegram:
Telegram can send each new inquiry to you, a group, or a channel. You own the bot.

## What to do

In DealerGrid, open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**.

1. In Telegram, message **@BotFather**, send `/newbot`, and save the bot token.
2. Find your chat ID with **@userinfobot** (your user ID, or the group/channel ID).
3. Send any message to your new bot so it can reply.
4. In DealerGrid, paste the bot token and chat ID, then save.

## If nothing arrives

- Start the bot with any message first.
- Confirm the chat ID and that the bot is in the group or channel.
- If the token was revoked, ask BotFather for a new one.

See [Choose how you hear about new inquiries](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
connections-webhook:
A webhook sends the full inquiry to an HTTPS URL as a JSON POST. Use it for Zapier, Make, Slack, or your CRM.

## What to do

In DealerGrid, open **Settings → How you hear about new inquiries → Optional delivery methods**.

1. Create a catch-hook URL in Zapier, Make, or your server.
2. Paste it into How you hear about new inquiries → Webhook and save.
3. Send a test inquiry and map the fields.

The URL must be HTTPS and return a 2xx within 10 seconds.

## What gets posted

```
POST https://your-endpoint.example.com/leads
Content-Type: application/json
X-Dealer-Signature: sha256=…  (only if you set a secret)
```

```json
{
  "event": "lead.captured",
  "leadId": "clxxx...",
  "platformSlug": "consumer-marketplace",
  "dealerName": "Prairie Ridge Motors",
  "vehicleRef": "Stock #DM-2024-042",
  "contact": {
    "name": "Alex Johnson",
    "email": "alex@example.com",
    "phone": "+15551234567",
    "message": "Is this still available?"
  }
}
```

Blank contact fields are omitted.

## Signing secret

If you enter a secret, each request includes `X-Dealer-Signature: sha256=<hmac>`. Verify with `HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw_body)`. Rotate the secret by saving a new value.

See [Choose how you hear about new inquiries](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
crm-delivery:
## Open the delivery details

On **Leads**, use the inquiry's CRM action to inspect its delivery details. A CRM (customer relationship management system) is separate from DealerGrid's shared inbox and the team's lead status.

## Choose the next step

| Recorded outcome | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| Not sent | Check the destination and use **Send to CRM** when available. |
| Sending | Wait for the attempt to finish before submitting another. |
| Accepted by mail server | Check the receiving CRM's inbox or activity. Acceptance does not prove that the CRM imported the inquiry. |
| Failed or did not finish | Read the attempt's error and correct the cause. Use **Retry send** only when available and appropriate. |
| Sending unavailable | Read the blocker. Review CRM lead routing in Channels or use the manual handoff options. |

## Manual handoff

Use **Copy Lead Summary** for a salesperson to enter the inquiry manually. Raw XML and file download are for systems or staff that accept that format. Check which route the receiver needs; copying or downloading does not transmit the lead.

## Confirm receipt

Confirm the inquiry in the receiving CRM. If the mail server accepted the lead but the CRM has no record, provide the receiving administrator with the destination address, attempt time, and lead identifier. Check for an existing record before choosing **Send again** to avoid duplicates.
dealerships-dealer-context:
Everything you see — vehicles, destinations, and leads — belongs to one dealership record.

## What to do

Before you import or connect a destination, read the dealership name in the header. If you work more than one dealership, switch dealerships first.

A group with three stores has three separate destination connections. CarGurus can be connected at Store 1 and not at Store 2.

Vehicles imported under one dealership will not appear on destinations connected under another.
dealerships-setup-and-handoff:
Internal staff use one dealership record to manage setup, people, inventory and activity. Each unfinished step explains what needs to happen next.

## Work through setup

1. Confirm the dealership’s details and assigned internal contact.
2. Invite the owner and check whether the invitation was emailed or needs to be shared.
3. Add representative inventory, including a price and photos. If there is no stock yet, mark **Waiting for stock**; the dealership stays in setup.
4. Complete destination setup and publish a vehicle to Auto Marketplace. A saved Autopilot preference does not publish a listing.
5. Confirm the owner has signed in and a marketplace inquiry has reached this dealership’s shared Leads inbox.

## Launch and handoff are separate

Launch records confirmed publication on Auto Marketplace. Handoff records that the owner can take over daily work and that the shared inbox has received an inquiry. A dealership can have a live listing while handoff is still waiting on the owner or inbox check.

The checks come from saved results, so staff do not tick them complete by hand. If a step is blocked, read its next action. Completing handoff does not turn on an external provider or prove that email, text-message or customer-management-system alerts were delivered.

Use **Open dealer view** to see the dealership’s daily screens while remaining signed in as yourself. The support banner shows which dealership you are helping and provides a return link.

Read [Invitations and sign-in help](doc:app/team-access) or [How new-inquiry alerts work](doc:connections/lead-notifications).
documentation-records:
## Record contract

Each published Markdown record explicitly declares `visibility: public` and has a permanent `id`, a stable `feature` identifier, one `type`, an `audience` list, a title, a summary, tags, synonyms, related document IDs, and a review date. Optional `implementation` entries name repository files. IDs and feature identifiers describe capabilities, not route names or storage folders.

The four types are **feature**, **task**, **troubleshooting**, and **reference**. Audience labels describe who benefits; they are not access controls. The published corpus is public. Export rejects missing or nonpublic visibility; keep internal runbooks and sensitive implementation material outside this corpus. Do not include credentials, customer records, or internal-only information.

## When implementation changes

1. Find documentation by feature, synonyms, or implementation path.
2. Check whether the capability's inputs, outputs, permissions, side effects, or failure behavior changed.
3. Update the feature record and affected tasks together. Match visible control labels in task instructions; keep durable behavior in feature records.
4. Preserve document IDs. If replacing a record, retain its old ID as an alias on the replacement and update related links.
5. Run help integrity tests and export the machine-readable index. Check that related IDs and implementation references resolve.

## Agent use

Read the feature record for intended behavior, then consult implementation references and tests for current behavior. Documentation describes the product; it does not authorize deployments or privileged operations. Report disagreement between code and documentation instead of silently treating either as proof.

From the repository root, run `node scripts/export-documentation.mjs` for JSON records including article bodies. The export uses the same metadata contract as the application and can be indexed by development tools.
industry-dms-source-of-truth:
Most rooftops keep inventory in a DMS, on the website, and in DealerGrid. Destinations receive the copy stored here.

## What to do

- Import or edit here when the price or status you want advertised changes.
- Mark sold here the same day the DMS shows sold, or the unit stays advertised.
- Use regular DMS exports so new units are not missing.

After an import, the file’s price is what we send until the next change. The DMS remains authoritative for floorplanning, deal jackets, and in-store process.

See [Import a spreadsheet](doc:inventory/csv-import) and [The price on a site does not match Vehicles](doc:troubleshooting/price-mismatch).
industry-oem-program-feeds:
Franchise rooftops often send inventory to a manufacturer program as well as classified sites. Those programs add brand rules.

## How they differ

| | Manufacturer program | Classified site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Setup | Usually a partner or OEM portal | Sign in or add the details they ask for |
| Fields | Brand trim and program codes | Broader list |
| Review | Program audits | Site policy |

A destination that says waiting on partner usually needs a contract on file before sends start.

DealerGrid does not certify co-op language. Marketing still owns CPO, APR, and photo-composition rules.

See [Advertising rules you still own](doc:law/advertising-disclaimers).
industry-photo-standards:
A vehicle cannot be listed until it has enough photos. Destinations can still reject a listing that passed that minimum.

## What to do

1. Add real photos of this VIN — not a title scan as the only image.
2. Put the front three-quarter shot first.
3. If a destination still rejects the listing, add the extra interior or background they ask for.

Units in recon often stay at Cannot list until the photographer finishes. Price and VIN can be correct the whole time.

See [When a vehicle can be listed](doc:inventory/inventory-readiness).
industry-syndication-lag:
Sent is not the same moment a buyer sees the change.

## Typical timing

| Stage | How long |
| --- | --- |
| DealerGrid sends | Seconds to minutes |
| They pick up the file or request | 15 minutes to several hours |
| Their search index refreshes | Extra delay on some sites |

Direct destinations can appear in minutes when they are not rate-limited. File-based destinations often wait for a 15–60 minute pickup. Some manufacturer programs run overnight.

Updating in DealerGrid ends when our work finishes. Connected or Sent does not mean every field is already public.

See [A sold vehicle is still on a site](doc:troubleshooting/sold-listing-still-live).
industry-vin-decode-limits:
A 17-character VIN can fill year, make, model, and sometimes trim. It does not finish every field destinations require.

## Often still blank

| Field | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Cab / bed | Decode style may not match the destination’s list |
| Packages | Options are often not in the VIN |
| Color | VIN does not store paint |
| Mileage | Never from the VIN |

A vehicle can decode cleanly and still be Cannot list for body style or photo count. Fill the gap on the vehicle or in the import file.

See [The vehicle looks complete but cannot be listed](doc:troubleshooting/blocked-but-complete).
inventory-bulk-edit:
Use bulk edit when selected vehicles should share the same value. Entering a price sets that exact price on every selected vehicle; it does not subtract a discount.

## What to do

1. Select the vehicles on Vehicles.
2. Fill in the fields you want to change. Available fields depend on the inventory category and can include price, mileage, condition, colors, and body style. Blank fields stay unchanged.
3. Choose **Apply**. Use **Clear** to clear the selection and entered values without applying them.

Photos and VIN are not bulk-edited. Open each vehicle or re-import those.

## What happens next

DealerGrid rechecks the lot and can send ready vehicles again. Vehicles that still cannot be listed stay held until their own problem is fixed. A price change does not skip a missing photo.
inventory-csv-import:
Open **Vehicles → Import spreadsheet**. Drop one CSV, TSV or text file into the upload area, choose a file, or paste rows copied from a spreadsheet. The first row must contain column names.

## Match the columns

Match your file’s headers to the inventory fields. Review suggested matches rather than assuming every column was recognized.

Include stock number, VIN, year, make, model, mileage, price, condition and exterior color. Add photo URLs if they are available. Use a full, accurate VIN; the preview explains any format problem. Keep stock numbers stable because they identify vehicles to update.

## Review and correct rows

1. Choose **Preview** to check the file without saving inventory changes.
2. Choose **Edit row** to correct a value in place. You can also go back to change column matches.
3. After editing, choose **Check corrected rows**. Import stays unavailable until the server checks the changes again.
4. Review which rows will create, update or skip a vehicle. You can skip a valid row you do not want to import.
5. Choose **Import** when the results match your intent.

A blocked row is skipped rather than saved. Corrected rows must pass the checks; editing a value alone does not make them valid.

## After importing

Review the result and inventory list. Imported values can replace existing vehicle details, including price and supplied photos. Review the preview before re-importing a file; stable stock numbers prevent accidental new records but do not protect existing values from updates.

Importing does not confirm publication. Review the vehicle’s listing status and its destinations next.

Read [Fix import errors](doc:troubleshooting/import-errors) and [Prepare vehicles for listing](doc:inventory/inventory-readiness).
inventory-import:
## What this feature does

Spreadsheet import maps file columns to inventory fields, validates rows, and creates or updates records. Preview is separate from committing changes.

## Inputs and identity

The first row contains column names. Existing vehicles are matched by dealership and stock number. A stock number is not freed when an old vehicle is sold or removed. Reusing it for another vehicle can target the wrong record.

## Outcomes and limits

Rows can create, update, skip, or fail. An import can change some rows while others do not save. Supplied values can overwrite existing data. Import completion does not establish publication on any destination.

For the step-by-step workflow, read [Import and correct a spreadsheet](doc:inventory-csv-import). For a failed row, read [Fix import errors](doc:troubleshooting-import-errors).
inventory-inventory-readiness:
A saved vehicle is not automatically listed. It can sit on Vehicles until it has a price, photos, and a connected destination.

## What the status means

| Status | Meaning | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ready to send | Required details are present | Send it, or leave Autopilot on for selected destinations |
| Needs details | Some destinations may still reject it | Add the extra fields or photos they ask for |
| Cannot list | A required item is missing | Fix price, photos, VIN, or availability |

## Destinations first

Channels controls which sites can receive vehicles. Only connected destinations appear as options on a vehicle. Your DealerGrid storefront is the first one to turn on because you do not sign in to another company.

## Ready to send is not published

Turning a vehicle ready, or checking a destination on that vehicle, does not put it live. It only means DealerGrid is allowed to send it. A listing is sent after you send it or Autopilot sends it. Sent is not a verified-live confirmation.

## After you fix a vehicle

Save the row. Ready vehicles can go out on the next send. Sold, removed, or zero-price vehicles may be excluded from new publication. Check the removal result for existing listings; an inventory change does not prove an external site has removed them.

See [Needs details vs cannot list](doc:inventory/warnings-vs-blocked) and [Sending updates automatically](doc:processes/auto-sync).
inventory-older-inventory:
The inventory age panel groups vehicles by time recorded in DealerGrid. Choose a group to review those vehicles.

A suggested price is a recommendation, not an automatic change or a guaranteed sale. Check the vehicle’s condition, costs and current asking price before applying it.

## Change a price deliberately

1. In Vehicles, open the available price suggestion and review its current price, proposed price, and reduction. Days in DealerGrid may differ from the time the vehicle has physically been on your lot.
2. Choose the displayed **Apply** price action only if it matches your dealership’s pricing decision. Choose **Keep Current Price** to leave the price unchanged.
3. Check the saved price in Vehicles and then the listing results on Channels.

Saving a price updates DealerGrid’s inventory. Publication depends on the destination’s supported delivery method and settings. It does not guarantee an immediate update or a price-drop badge on every website.

Read [A website shows a different price](doc:troubleshooting/price-mismatch).
inventory-sold-removed:
Update a vehicle’s status when it is no longer available. Lowering its price to zero does not mark it sold.

## Mark a vehicle sold

Open the vehicle in **Vehicles** and choose **Mark sold**. Confirm that its status changes to **Sold**. This changes availability in DealerGrid; inspect the downstream listing result separately.

## Choose the right status

- **Sold:** the vehicle has been sold. Keep its record for your team’s history.
- **Removed:** the vehicle is no longer available through this dealership, for example after a transfer.

If another inventory system shows the vehicle as sold, check that the change also appears in DealerGrid.

## Check the listings

DealerGrid requests removal from the destinations it manages. A request is not confirmation that the destination has removed the listing. Check its latest result and follow any next step shown.

Listings created manually or through a separate provider may need to be removed there. Pausing Autopilot does not remove existing listings; removal work for managed listings can continue while paused.

See [A sold vehicle is still listed](doc:troubleshooting/sold-listing-still-live).
inventory-stock-number-rules:
Stock number is how DealerGrid finds a vehicle when you import or edit. Keep it the same while that unit is on the lot.

## What to do

- Use the same stock number the whole time the vehicle is here.
- Use a different stock number for a different vehicle, including when the old vehicle is sold or removed.
- Match your dealership management system (DMS) stock number when it uniquely identifies the same vehicle.

## After a unit leaves

Mark the old unit sold or removed and keep its stock number attached to that record. Spreadsheet imports match existing records by dealership and stock number, including old inventory. Closing out the old vehicle does not free its stock number for a new one. Review any row labeled as an update before importing.

See [Import a spreadsheet](doc:inventory/csv-import).
inventory-warnings-vs-blocked:
Vehicles uses two problem states. They are not the same as already sent.

## Cannot list

At least one required item is missing or invalid — no price, too few photos, a bad VIN, or a sold unit still marked available. DealerGrid will not send that vehicle until you fix it.

## Needs details

Something should be improved — photo quality, optional trim, or a stricter site’s extra fields. The vehicle can still be sent to destinations that do not require those extras.

## What to do

Open the vehicle. The next action tells you what is missing. After you save, ready vehicles can be sent again. Ready to send is not the same as already live on the site.

See [When a vehicle can be listed](doc:inventory/inventory-readiness).
law-advertising-disclaimers:
What you advertise is still your responsibility. DealerGrid can block a missing VIN or photo count. It does not interpret state fee rules or OEM co-op language.

## What to do

- Put the obtainable asking price in the price field. Doc fees and conditional rebates belong in the disclosure your state requires.
- Mark sold or removed the day the deal funds. Do not leave a funded unit available.
- Use photos of the actual vehicle. Stock art or last year’s body style is treated as misrepresentation on several sites.
- Hold a listing if compliance has not approved the copy.

A vehicle can be ready to send here and still fail a destination’s own review.

See [Mark a vehicle sold or removed](doc:inventory/sold-removed).
platforms-account-states:
The destination account is this dealership’s relationship with that company. Sends do not start until the account allows them.

## Dealership-facing states

| What you see | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Connected | Account setup is recorded. Check supported delivery methods and remaining requirements; this is not confirmation of a live listing. |
| Not connected / Sign-in needed | You still need to sign in or add details. |
| Waiting on partner | They have the details and still need to accept. |
| Could not connect | Check connection, or ask support. |

Internal records may still store Active, Account needed, Credentials needed, Partner required, Pending review, Blocked, or Suspended. Those are the same ideas with operator names.

## Who operates the relationship

| Class | Typical setup |
| --- | --- |
| Owned | Your DealerGrid storefront — no outside sign-in |
| They receive listings | File or partner connection after they accept |
| Assisted | An agency posts for the dealership |
| Partner dependent | A contract must be on file before sends |

Fix the destination on Channels. Changing photos does not change connection state. After setup, confirm that the destination supports the update method you need. For automatic updates, it must also be selected in Autopilot.
platforms-credential-rotation:
A destination may require you to reconnect when a sign-in expires, a key is revoked, or account permissions change. Check the connection result rather than assuming every password change breaks every integration.

## What to do

1. Open that destination on Channels.
2. Sign in again, or ask support to enter the new file-transfer details.
3. Use the connection-check action if the destination provides one, and review its result.

Do not re-import inventory to fix a sign-in problem. After reconnecting, check the delivery method and Autopilot selection before expecting another update.
platforms-platform:
A destination is a marketplace or advertising site that can receive this dealership’s vehicles.

## What DealerGrid stores

| Record | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Profile | Required fields, photo minimums, price rules |
| Account | This rooftop’s connection, sign-in, and standing |
| Send result | Combined outcome of the account plus each vehicle |

The same vehicle can pass on one destination and fail on another.

## How updates leave the server

**They receive a file.** Vehicles are batched and picked up on that company’s schedule. Delay of 15–60 minutes is common.

**We send directly.** Each vehicle or small batch is posted. Errors come back per stock number.

Dealership users connect the destination and keep vehicle details current. File names and tokens stay with support.

See [When a destination can receive vehicles](doc:processes/platform-readiness).
processes-approval-holds:
A destination can be connected and still wait for approval before the first send or a large refresh.

## What to do

1. Open that destination on Channels.
2. Read the next action. If it says someone must approve, finish that step there or with your contact at that company.
3. Leave other destinations alone — a hold on one site does not stop the others.

## What happens next

When the hold clears, ready vehicles can go out on the next send. Inventory can look ready the whole time; the destination was the thing waiting.
processes-auto-sync:
Autopilot checks inventory changes and updates supported destinations you have selected. It does not make every connected account an automatic destination.

## Before turning it on

Review the selected destinations and any setup problems. Only destinations shown as available for automatic updates can be included. Other destinations may require a manual update or help from their provider.

Vehicles must also pass the relevant listing checks. Missing details and unusual changes can stop an update until someone reviews the problem. Follow the owner and next action shown on the issue.

## What pausing does

Pausing stops new publication work managed by Autopilot. Removal of sold or removed listings it manages continues. Listings placed manually may need a separate removal action.

Auto Marketplace reads current inventory details. Pausing does not freeze prices or other fields on listings that are already public. Use the appropriate listing or vehicle action if you need a vehicle removed.

## Check the result

A preview estimates what would happen using current data; it does not publish anything. A submitted update is not proof that a destination is already showing it. Look for a confirmed live or removed result.

Read [Connect a destination](doc:app/channels) or [A sold vehicle is still listed](doc:troubleshooting/sold-listing-still-live).
processes-platform-readiness:
A destination is a marketplace or advertising site where you want vehicles to appear. A connected account alone does not confirm automatic updates are available.

## Before sending

1. Open **Channels** and finish the destination’s setup. Follow any sign-in or partner approval step shown.
2. Check its update method. Automatic, manual, and partner-managed destinations have different next steps. For Autopilot, the destination must support automatic updates and be selected.
3. Open **Vehicles** and resolve the missing details shown for that destination. Requirements can differ by site.
4. After sending, check the result. Submitted updates may still need processing; only a confirmed live result establishes that the listing was checked.

See [Connect a destination](doc:app/channels) and [When a vehicle can be listed](doc:inventory/inventory-readiness).
processes-sync-status:
Send status is a snapshot for the selected dealership. It is not a full event log.

## Run phases

| Phase | State | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Idle | No active send | No send is queued. Destinations may still be processing an earlier update. |
| Scheduled | Updating | A save just finished; the send is about to start. |
| Running | Updating | Checking vehicles or sending now. |
| Failed | Needs fix | The run stopped. Fix the vehicle or destination, then save again. |

Updating ends when DealerGrid finishes — not when Cars.com already shows the new price.

## Counts

**Ready to send** — vehicles that pass checks and can be included.

**Cannot list** — vehicles with a required problem. They stay in inventory but are not sent.

**Destinations ready** — connected destinations that can receive at least one ready vehicle.

**Destinations blocked** — connection, sign-in, partner, or approval gaps. Vehicle edits alone do not clear these.

The last-activity line is the most recent send milestone, not every field edit.
staff-dealership-assistance:
## What this feature does

The dealership directory is a work list. Each record brings together setup progress, destination connections, people, and activity for that business. Internal support staff see the dealerships they are allowed to assist; site administrators have additional site-wide tools.

## Find the next action

1. Open **Dealerships**, search for the business, and confirm its identity before opening the record. Use **Mine** when you want records assigned to you and that filter is available.
2. Read the record's current state and next action. **Overview**, **Channels**, **People**, and **Activity** cover different parts of the same dealership.
3. Check responsibility before acting. **Dealership** means the dealership must supply or correct something; **Our team** means internal staff; **Partner** means an external provider; **System** means processing owned by DealerGrid. **Unassigned** does not identify a responsible person.
4. Open the relevant section and complete the available action within your permissions. Use **Open dealer view** when you need the dealership-facing screens. Confirm the dealership in the support banner and use its return link when finished.

## Check completion

Review the saved result and the current next action. A successfully saved setting does not establish that a downstream listing or notification completed. Use Activity to inspect recorded events where relevant.

## When you cannot proceed

If the record or action is unavailable, ask an authorized site administrator to check your assignment or role. For another team's task, share the dealership, affected feature, error, and expected next action. Do not send credentials. Do not change a different dealership or a shared setting to work around missing access.
staff-integration-setup:
## Choose the correct scope

A dealership's channel connection belongs to that dealership. Site administration's **Settings → Destinations we support** controls shared destination availability and integration settings. Do not change shared configuration to repair one dealership without evidence that the shared configuration is the problem.

## Check the connection

1. Open the affected dealership's channel and read its setup state, delivery method, and next action.
2. Check whether the missing information belongs to that dealership or to the shared integration. A provider contract or account permission cannot be fixed by editing vehicle photos.
3. For a dealership account, use its available setup or reconnection action. For a shared integration, an authorized site administrator should inspect **Destinations we support** and the relevant destination.
4. Review the saved connection result, then separately check whether automatic updates are supported and selected.

## Expected result

The connection should no longer show the original setup problem. Publication still depends on vehicle requirements, supported delivery, and downstream processing. A saved credential is not a confirmed live listing.

## If setup still fails

Record the destination, affected dealership, time, and error. Never copy tokens or passwords into a support message. Follow the provider-specific configuration reference when available; do not assume every destination supports the same transport or authorization method.
staff-problems:
## Start with the scope

Site administrators use **Problems → Actionable Issues** for issues across dealerships. Staff with a narrower workspace use the affected dealership and its activity or channel details. A missing site-wide menu does not grant permission to access it another way.

## Diagnose before retrying

1. Confirm the dealership, vehicle or destination associated with the issue. The scope tells you whether you are looking at one record or all dealerships.
2. Read the failure and available action. Missing inventory details require an inventory correction; expired authorization requires reconnection. Repeating a send does not repair either.
3. Use the offered recovery action only after the prerequisite is corrected. Avoid bulk retry when different issues have different causes.
4. Read the returned outcome and inspect **Audit Log** or dealership Activity for recorded attempts. A completed retry is not proof that an external website has published the listing.

## When to involve someone else

For dealership data or access, contact the responsible dealership person. For shared integration configuration, involve an authorized site administrator. For a provider-side requirement, involve that provider. Include scope, error text, attempt time, and steps already taken.

An issue-list loading error is not an all-clear result. Retry loading before concluding that there are no open issues.
staff-settings:
## Scope and access

Site administration Settings is for authorized site administrators. Dealership **Settings** controls one business's profile, people, and notifications. Internal support staff may not have access to site-wide administration.

| Site-wide tool | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Destinations we support | Shared destination availability and integration configuration |
| Is DealerGrid up | System status information |
| Who can sign in | Internal staff accounts and dealership assignments |
| Recent changes | Recorded staff changes across the site |

## Before changing a setting

Confirm whether the requested change affects one dealership or the entire service. Use the dealership record for dealership work. Review the action's scope and consequence before saving a site-wide change.

## Check the outcome

Read the save result and inspect the affected record or recent changes. A successful configuration save does not prove that a sign-in, send, or external integration has recovered; check that specific operation separately.
troubleshooting-blocked-but-complete:
Cannot list means at least one required check failed. The row can still show year, make, model, and photos.

## What to do

1. Open the vehicle and read the next action.
2. Check VIN, price, photo count, body style, and whether it is still available.
3. Remember a vehicle can be ready to send to one destination and held on another that needs extra fields.

VIN decode often leaves cab type, bed length, or body style blank. Fill those by hand if the destination asks for them.

See [Needs details vs cannot list](doc:inventory/warnings-vs-blocked).
troubleshooting-import-errors:
The preview explains problems before any inventory changes are saved. Choose **Edit row** to fix a value, then **Check corrected rows**. If the wrong field was matched, go back to the column-matching step.

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Missing stock number | Match the stock-number column and enter a value. |
| Invalid VIN | Check the original VIN for missing characters or a typing error. Do not guess the missing characters. |
| Missing price or mileage | Check both the value and the column match. |
| Duplicate stock number | Keep one row for each vehicle in the file. |
| Required field still missing | Check whether its column was ignored or matched to another field. |

## If only some rows save

Review the import result. Skipped or failed rows did not save successfully; other rows may already have been created or updated. Correct the affected rows and preview them again before importing. Avoid repeatedly submitting the whole file without checking what already changed.

If an unexpected error continues, give support the stock number, the action you tried and the error shown. Do not include passwords or connection secrets.

Read [Import and correct a spreadsheet](doc:inventory/csv-import).
troubleshooting-price-mismatch:
A site shows the last price it accepted from DealerGrid. That can differ from your DMS or website if those were changed somewhere else.

## What to do

1. Confirm the asking price on Vehicles is the price you want sent.
2. If you only changed the DMS, update the price here or import again.
3. Open the destination on Channels and confirm the last update went through.
4. Wait for that site’s own refresh. Sent is not the same as already visible.

Doc fees and conditional rebates belong in the disclosure, not hidden inside the asking price. See [Advertising rules you still own](doc:law/advertising-disclaimers).
troubleshooting-sold-listing-still-live:
First check that the correct vehicle is marked **Sold** or **Removed** in the correct dealership. A price of zero is not a substitute for changing its status.

## Check the affected destination

Open Channels and review the listing’s result and next action. A request to remove a listing is not the same as confirmation that it has disappeared. Connection problems or the destination’s processing schedule can delay removal.

The sold-listing check compares DealerGrid’s inventory and listing records. A clean result means those records agree; it does not independently inspect every external website.

## If the listing is still public

- Check whether DealerGrid manages the listing or someone posted it manually.
- Use the supported removal action and review its result.
- For a manual or partner-managed listing, remove it with that provider or ask the person responsible to do so.
- If a removal fails or remains unconfirmed, give support the stock number and destination. Follow the next action rather than assuming another wait will fix it.

Read [Mark a vehicle sold or removed](doc:inventory/sold-removed) and [Automatic updates and pausing](doc:processes/auto-sync).
